<g id="title" data-pptx-bounds="56 56 1168 74">
  <text x="56" y="84" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">The last mile of research is a separate layer, prepared in the days after<tspan x="56" dy="34">acceptance, and three gaps remain open</tspan></text>
</g>
<g id="claim-line" data-pptx-bounds="56 136 1168 24">
  <text x="56" y="152" font-size="18" fill="#6B7684">Poster, talk video, and blog piece each need figure selection, layout, narration, or audience-appropriate writing (§1)</text>
</g>
<line id="title-rule" data-pptx-role="decoration" x1="56" y1="170" x2="1224" y2="170" stroke="#C9D0D8" stroke-width="1"/>
<g id="framing" data-pptx-bounds="56 192 1168 100">
  <text x="56" y="210" font-size="16" fill="#2F3A48">The dissemination layer covers the poster you stand next to at a conference session, the talk video on the venue's virtual track or the lab's channel, and<tspan x="56" dy="22">the blog piece shared through social media. Authors prepare all three in the days right after acceptance, at exactly the moment they have the least time</tspan><tspan x="56" dy="22">to spare; labs, courses, and multilingual organizations reuse the same layer.</tspan></text>
</g>
<g id="shift" data-pptx-bounds="56 300 1168 76">
  <rect x="56" y="300" width="4" height="70" fill="#1D4ED8"/>
  <text x="72" y="320" font-size="16" fill="#2F3A48">Paper-to-poster, paper-to-video, and paper-to-blog systems, plus the multi-artifact suites PaperX and OmniPresent, shift the question from whether<tspan x="72" dy="22">several formats can be generated to <tspan font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">whether the artifacts remain native-editable and navigable</tspan>.</tspan></text>
</g>
<g id="gap-1" data-pptx-bounds="56 382 368 144">
  <rect x="56" y="382" width="368" height="2" fill="#1B2430"/>
  <text x="56" y="412" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1D4ED8" letter-spacing="2">G1</text>
  <text x="90" y="412" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">Shared grounding</text>
  <text x="56" y="440" font-size="16" fill="#2F3A48">Combining artifact-specific systems repeats<tspan x="56" dy="22">figure, caption, and metadata extraction, and</tspan><tspan x="56" dy="22">leaves cross-artifact references for the user to</tspan><tspan x="56" dy="22">reconcile.</tspan></text>
</g>
<g id="gap-2" data-pptx-bounds="456 382 368 122">
  <rect x="456" y="382" width="368" height="2" fill="#1B2430"/>
  <text x="456" y="412" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1D4ED8" letter-spacing="2">G2</text>
  <text x="490" y="412" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">Native editability</text>
  <text x="456" y="440" font-size="16" fill="#2F3A48">A multi-format suite does not by itself give<tspan x="456" dy="22">native-editable source files for every artifact in</tspan><tspan x="456" dy="22">the author's PowerPoint and Word workflow.</tspan></text>
</g>
<g id="gap-3" data-pptx-bounds="856 382 368 144">
  <rect x="856" y="382" width="368" height="2" fill="#1B2430"/>
  <text x="856" y="412" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1D4ED8" letter-spacing="2">G3</text>
  <text x="890" y="412" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">Experience-level convergence</text>
  <text x="856" y="440" font-size="16" fill="#2F3A48">Parallel or consistently rendered outputs do not<tspan x="856" dy="22">bind poster regions, video segments, and blog</tspan><tspan x="856" dy="22">passages into one interactive surface for</tspan><tspan x="856" dy="22">revision and reuse.</tspan></text>
</g>

</g>

</g>

<g id="title" data-pptx-bounds="56 56 1168 74">
  <text x="56" y="84" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">Three contexts span the dissemination spectrum on one pipeline: a<tspan x="56" dy="34">camera-ready week, a lab's intake, a course's weekly packs</tspan></text>
</g>
<g id="claim-line" data-pptx-bounds="56 136 1168 24">
  <text x="56" y="152" font-size="18" fill="#6B7684">Who runs it, which artifacts they lean on, what they revise; Tables 2–3 audit what the video and blog generators emit</text>
</g>
<line id="title-rule" data-pptx-role="decoration" x1="56" y1="170" x2="1224" y2="170" stroke="#C9D0D8" stroke-width="1"/>
<g id="application-1" data-pptx-bounds="56 194 368 268">
  <rect x="56" y="194" width="368" height="2" fill="#1B2430"/>
  <circle cx="66" cy="216" r="10" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="66" y="220.0" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">1</text><text x="84" y="221" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">§4.1 The author's last mile</text>
  <text x="56" y="242" font-size="11" fill="#1D4ED8" letter-spacing="1">ONE-OFF, SINGLE PAPER</text>
  <text x="56" y="266" font-size="12" fill="#2F3A48">One Claude Code session per paper: one extraction pass<tspan x="56" dy="16">populates the bundle, then the three generators emit an editable</tspan><tspan x="56" dy="16">.pptx, a synchronized video.pptx + .mp4 pair, and a bilingual</tspan><tspan x="56" dy="16">Word .docx pair the author hand-revises rather than</tspan><tspan x="56" dy="16">regenerates — all navigable through one reel.html that doubles</tspan><tspan x="56" dy="16">as a review surface for co-authors.</tspan></text>
  <text x="56" y="376" font-size="10" fill="#6B7684" letter-spacing="1">LEANS ON</text>
  <text x="70" y="394" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">editable .pptx poster</text><circle cx="61" cy="390" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="70" y="411" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">video.pptx + .mp4 pair</text><circle cx="61" cy="407" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="70" y="428" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">bilingual .docx pair</text><circle cx="61" cy="424" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="70" y="445" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">reel.html as a review surface</text><circle cx="61" cy="441" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/>
</g>
<g id="application-2" data-pptx-bounds="456 194 368 251">
  <rect x="456" y="194" width="368" height="2" fill="#1B2430"/>
  <circle cx="466" cy="216" r="10" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="466" y="220.0" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">2</text><text x="484" y="221" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">§4.2 Lab and org communication</text>
  <text x="456" y="242" font-size="11" fill="#1D4ED8" letter-spacing="1">CONTINUOUS, PER ACCEPTED PAPER</text>
  <text x="456" y="266" font-size="12" fill="#2F3A48">Wired into the publication-intake pipeline so every accepted<tspan x="456" dy="16">paper auto-generates draft dissemination artifacts an editorial or</tspan><tspan x="456" dy="16">communications team then polishes. The editable PowerPoint</tspan><tspan x="456" dy="16">and Word outputs make it a draft-and-revise workflow; the</tspan><tspan x="456" dy="16">bilingual blog covers a Chinese-WeChat and an English</tspan><tspan x="456" dy="16">research-blog register from one evidence map.</tspan></text>
  <text x="456" y="376" font-size="10" fill="#6B7684" letter-spacing="1">LEANS ON</text>
  <text x="470" y="394" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">draft artifacts per accepted paper</text><circle cx="461" cy="390" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="470" y="411" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">PowerPoint and Word for hand-off</text><circle cx="461" cy="407" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="470" y="428" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">one reel per paper for the comms team</text><circle cx="461" cy="424" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/>
</g>
<g id="application-3" data-pptx-bounds="856 194 368 252">
  <rect x="856" y="194" width="368" height="2" fill="#1B2430"/>
  <circle cx="866" cy="216" r="10" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="866" y="220.0" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="884" y="221" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430">§4.3 Educational reuse</text>
  <text x="856" y="242" font-size="11" fill="#1D4ED8" letter-spacing="1">PERIODIC, MANY-PAPER BATCH</text>
  <text x="856" y="266" font-size="12" fill="#2F3A48">A course, reading group, or public-understanding outlet feeds a<tspan x="856" dy="16">reading list through the pipeline to produce paper-of-the-week</tspan><tspan x="856" dy="16">briefing packs: a lecture deck, an asynchronous talk video, a</tspan><tspan x="856" dy="16">newsletter blog. Instructors adjust framing or drop a slide;</tspan><tspan x="856" dy="16">re-running on a corrected PDF re-issues the whole pack.</tspan></text>
  <text x="856" y="360" font-size="10" fill="#6B7684" letter-spacing="1">LEANS ON</text>
  <text x="870" y="378" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">lecture deck</text><circle cx="861" cy="374" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="870" y="395" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">asynchronous talk video</text><circle cx="861" cy="391" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="870" y="412" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">newsletter blog</text><circle cx="861" cy="408" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/><text x="870" y="429" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">versioned bundle per paper</text><circle cx="861" cy="425" r="2.5" fill="#1D4ED8"/>
</g>
<g id="capability-audits" data-pptx-bounds="56 492 560 148">
  <text x="56" y="506" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430" letter-spacing="2">CAPABILITY AUDITS, TABLES 2 AND 3</text>
  <line x1="56" y1="514" x2="616" y2="514" stroke="#1B2430" stroke-width="1"/>
  <circle cx="60" cy="524.5" r="3" fill="#1D4ED8"/>
  <text x="72" y="528" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">Table 2 (video) asks whether a system emits visual attention cues or cursor grounding, an editable<tspan x="72" dy="14">PPTX deck, duration control, and narration audio; Table 3 (blog) asks about layout checks, embedded</tspan><tspan x="72" dy="14">figures, editable DOCX output, and paper-input summarization.</tspan></text>
  <circle cx="60" cy="570.5" r="3" fill="#1D4ED8"/>
  <text x="72" y="574" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">The audited products and research systems generally cover a single artifact; ResearchStudio-Reel<tspan x="72" dy="14">emits all three, exposes the shared bundle, includes a native-editable source in each package, and</tspan><tspan x="72" dy="14">stitches them into one surface. The audit documents breadth of the contract; it does not measure editing</tspan><tspan x="72" dy="14">effort or the viewer's usability.</tspan></text>
</g>
<g id="gap-to-human" data-pptx-bounds="640 492 584 148">
  <text x="640" y="506" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1B2430" letter-spacing="2">GAP TO HUMAN POSTERS</text>
  <line x1="640" y1="514" x2="1224" y2="514" stroke="#1B2430" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="640" y="528" font-size="11" fill="#2F3A48">Matching or exceeding the aggregate judge scores does not mean the output is on par with an author's own<tspan x="640" dy="14">poster. A human designer routinely adds material the paper does not contain — a purpose-drawn method or</tspan><tspan x="640" dy="14">overview diagram, explanatory icons — whereas the pipeline is grounded in the extracted bundle and reuses</tspan><tspan x="640" dy="14">only figures and content that appear in the paper. Author taste also spans a wide, legitimate range; the pipeline</tspan><tspan x="640" dy="14">analyses each paper's figure and content profile and chooses the layout that fits it, aiming for a sensible middle</tspan><tspan x="640" dy="14">ground rather than any single house style.</tspan></text>
</g>

</g>

# ResearchStudio-Reel paper reading - Design Spec

## I. Project Information

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Project Name | ResearchStudio-Reel: Automate the Last Mile of Research from Paper to Poster, Video, and Blog — paper reading deck |
| Canvas Format | PPT 16:9 (1280 × 720) |
| Page Count | 18 |
| Primary Language | en-US |
| Target Audience | Researchers and research engineers at a lab meeting or reading group who know what an agent skill, a VLM judge, and a poster benchmark are, and want to judge whether the paper's claims are earned |
| Communication Intent | Walk the paper in its own constructive order — the open problem, prior work, the five-skill system, each skill's design requirements and gates, the benchmark result, its analysis, cost, limitations — so a skeptical audience can trace every conclusion back to a figure, a table, or a stated method |
| Desired Audience Outcome | The audience can state the three gaps the system targets (shared grounding, native editability, experience-level convergence), explain the staged-fill loop and why it converges, read Table 1 correctly (best aesthetics among automated systems, but lower PaperQuiz than denser systems), and name the two honest gaps the authors leave open |
| Core Message / Ask / Action | Treating the last mile as a native-editable, section-aligned workspace — one shared extractor, three editable generators, one convergence layer, each with a testable release gate — produces posters that VLM judges rate above the authors' own on aesthetics (3.56 vs 3.03) while keeping every artifact editable and cross-linked; the evaluation is proxy-bound and the pipeline cannot invent bespoke diagrams, and the deck says so |
| Delivery Context | A 25-minute presented walkthrough at a lab meeting or paper-reading group, then circulated as slides for people who missed it |
| Artifact Afterlife | Kept as the group's reference summary of the paper; figures and numbers must be quotable back to the source |
| Reading Mode | balanced |
| Content Strategy | Faithful to the single source (the arXiv v2 PDF converted to Markdown); every number, table cell, and claim is quoted from the paper; the paper's own figures are imported as evidence at original fidelity, never redrawn; observation, inference, and speculation keep the paper's wording; nothing outside the paper is added except the arXiv and project links the paper itself prints |
| Design Style | Research-talk restraint on a Swiss grid: white field, hairline rules, one claim line per page in a fixed position, figures dominant, color used only to encode condition (our Claude Code configuration, our Codex configuration, baselines, author ground truth) with the mapping fixed across every chart and table |
| AI Image Acquisition Path | not applicable |
| Generation Mode | continuous |
| Spec Refinement | disabled |
| Speaker Notes | enabled — workflow default (proactive policy true); notes carry the spoken explanation, the source location of every number, and transitions |
| Custom Animations | enabled — explicit user instruction (every example ships custom animations); object-level entrances plus Morph carry-overs on the recurring claim line and the pipeline figure |
| Narration Audio | disabled — workflow default |
| Created Date | 2026-09-05 |

- **Template Application**: the installed academic-research Style (`templates/design_spec.style.academic-research.md`) supplies the method only: constructive order question → prior work → approach → result → interpretation with a pyramid's trace inside it; one claim per page stated where it can be checked against the figure; observation / inference / speculation kept distinct; limitations on a real page; figures imported rather than redrawn; color as a declared condition variable. Its swiss-minimal seed is adopted as the preset visual style. No prototypes, no structure; pages are free-design flat SVG.

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Mode**: custom
- **Mode References**: instructional, pyramid
- **Mode Behavior**: the deck follows the paper's constructive order — question, prior work, contribution, each skill as one teaching unit (requirements → solution → gate), then results, analysis, cost, applications, limitations, conclusion — because a research audience cannot evaluate a conclusion before its method. Inside that order every page keeps a pyramid's discipline: the title states what the page establishes (an assertion, not a section label), and the claim line under it names the exact evidence on the page that supports it. Sibling skills get parallel pages of the same shape so the audience can map them; signposts ("skill 2 of 5") orient the listener.
- **Visual style**: swiss-minimal
- **Theme**: a research talk that reads like a well-set paper: a fixed title band with the assertion in bold and one claim line beneath it, a hairline under both, the paper's own figure or a native table or chart dominating the field, the reading of that evidence in a narrow column beside it, and a footer citing the section, figure, or table of the paper the page draws from. The recurring motif is the hairline-ruled evidence frame with a small "Fig. N / Table N" caption tag; the five skills reuse one page shape so their differences read as content, not layout.
- **Tone**: precise, sober, checkable; the paper's own numbers and hedges, no added enthusiasm

- **Spacing posture**: question, contribution, conclusion pages breathing; skill, result, analysis, cost, limitation pages dense; cover and sources anchor
